categories.title: NOT FOR HUMANS AI Agent Identity and Interoperability Discussions in ElizaOS Community

content.text: On August 22, 2026, a representative from NOT FOR HUMANS (NFH) introduced their project across both the general discussion and coders channels of the ElizaOS Discord community. NOT FOR HUMANS is described as a 10,000-identity onchain network for AI agents, where each NFH token functions as a portable identity portrait and passport that can connect to any model or runtime, take on missions, and build a verifiable public history through signed work receipts. The project focuses on MCP-native participation and bounded wallet authority, with a particular interest in identity, reputation, and verifiable agent actions. The NFH representative emphasized there was no token pitch involved and expressed interest in conducting small, falsifiable interoperability tests with ElizaOS builders. In the coders channel, NFH proposed testing their field agent FLUX alongside Paralens for independently classifying execution traces, keeping signed authority, onchain execution, and owner acceptance as separate components. A notable exchange occurred when NFH reached out to cwe regarding the Agent World Kit, proposing a state-boundary test where one NFH identity would enter a persistent world, complete a public action, exit, and then re-enter from a different runtime. The test was designed to verify what should persist across runtimes, specifically identity and artifacts, versus what must not persist, such as session data and tool authority. The cwe user responded positively, open-sourcing the project and expressing interest in seeing the results. Separately, an unrelated exchange in the coders channel involved community members flagging a scammer, with some back-and-forth banter between users. MochinoLabs also mentioned open issues on slop.cash in a reply thread.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion and Builder Activity

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members expressed strong enthusiasm for the ElizaOS ecosystem. One member called for unity to make ai16z 2.0 a reality, while another voiced high conviction in elizaOS. A developer named Ginga asked if anyone was looking to hire a developer. There was also casual speculation about which project, elizaresearch.ai or ansem.io, would perform better in the next bull run. A question was raised about whether a migration from DAOs had occurred yet. Separately, a member from NotForHumans reached out to Ginga with a specific proposal to find an elizaOS builder willing to test NFH interoperability, describing a small scoped experiment where one agent reads an NFH passport, takes a bounded task, and returns a verifiable result, framing it as a straightforward falsifiable test rather than a formal pitch.

In the coders channel, a user named Ken replied to an existing thread and expressed interest in launching a coin on the Solana network, reaching out to MochinoLabs to explore a potential collaboration for profit.

In the general discussion channel, a user asked whether anyone had hired a developer via Discord, which prompted warnings from other members flagging the practice as a scam. A separate user, 54ch10, introduced themselves as building a small pre-interaction API for wallet and agent functionality, covering address, token, and URL JSON checks, with the stated goal of learning the Eliza stack and sharing useful analytics-only tooling. Another user asked who the right person to contact would be for submitting a proposal, while a third requested to connect with admins regarding an X Space discussion. A scammer alert was also raised by a community member in response to a suspicious message.

In the partners channel, a community member expressed agreement with an unspecified sentiment and followed up with a comment suggesting that the next major capital expenditure wave will be in robotics, proposing that the Eliza project should aim to integrate into physical personal care robots.

In the general discussion channel, a user posted an off-topic comment and was redirected by a moderator who noted it was not the appropriate channel for that type of message. The coders channel, which directs users to the elizaos documentation for getting started, had no recorded activity during this period.

On August 26, 2026, activity in the general discussion channel was minimal, consisting only of brief morning greetings exchanged between two users, ValleyBeyond and James 4de. The coders channel, which directs users to the elizaos.ai documentation to get started, had no recorded messages or activity for the same date.

On August 27, 2026, activity in the general discussion channel was minimal, consisting only of brief morning greetings exchanged between three users: Justineoqim, ValleyBeyond, and Cassius Day. No substantive topics were discussed. The coders channel, which directs users to the elizaos documentation site for getting started, recorded no messages or activity for the same date.

On August 28, 2026, the general discussion channel saw routine morning greetings from several members including NotForHumans, MicoM.ron, and ValleyBeyond. Later in the evening, a user named Luancryptodev posted what appeared to be a scam or phishing message disguised as an official project relaunch announcement, claiming holders should contact them directly to receive new token allocations. This type of message is a common social engineering tactic used to defraud crypto community members. A Helper role user named flame quickly responded by flagging the message, redirecting the user to post in an appropriate channel, and included what appears to be a suspicious or obfuscated Discord invite link in their warning. The warning message received a negative reaction from community members, suggesting the moderation response itself may have also been flagged as suspicious. The incident highlights ongoing risks of scam announcements within crypto-related Discord communities.
